While it notes a shift from requiring specialized GIS labs to making tools available to average responders, this represents additive capability enhancement and routine technology adoption, not the deliberate abandonment of an obsolete assumption or practice rooted in Katrina-identified failure. The text does not problematize a prior approach as harmful or call for dismantling an existing system; it simply describes improved access to tools. This falls clearly under the negative clarification for unlearning: 'The text only discusses...capacity expansion, or incremental improvement. The change is purely additive without rejecting prior assumptions.'
